title: One Event, One Penalty: Returned Payments and Late Fees on PracticePay Plans
content:
**Which payment and which due date.** On a PracticePay Patient Financing plan, the payment that came back is the payment entry that the returned-payment entry reverses, and the due date it was credited toward is the installment due date that payment entry names.

**Rule.** The one-penalty limit of a returned-payment fee follows the event the return belongs to: when the payment that came back was credited toward a monthly due date, is dated no later than the last day of that due date's grace period, and a late fee for that due date still stands on the plan after any waiver of it, the return and that late fee are one event, and the returned-payment fee is only the part of the product above that standing late fee, never below 0.00; when the payment that came back was credited toward a monthly due date and either is dated after the last day of that due date's grace period or no late fee for that due date still stands, the returned-payment fee is the product but never more than the plan's monthly payment amount; when the payment that came back was not credited toward any monthly due date, the product applies with no one-penalty limit; the grace period's last day being the due date plus the plan's late-fee grace days in calendar days, counted from the day after the due date.


"Still stands after any waiver" means the late fee charged for that due date less any waiver entry naming it is above 0.00.

## The three cases

| The payment that came back | Limit applied to the fee product |
|---|---|
| credited toward a due date, dated no later than its grace period's last day, a late fee for that due date still standing | only the part above the standing late fee, never below 0.00 |
| credited toward a due date, but dated after the grace period's last day, or no late fee for that due date standing | never more than the monthly payment amount |
| not credited toward any due date | none |

## Worked figures (hypothetical fee product 24.00, monthly payment 80.00, due date 1 March, grace period ending 11 March)

- Payment dated 5 March came back; a late fee of 20.00 for 1 March stands: 24.00 less 20.00, that is 4.00.
- Same, but the late fee was fully waived: no late fee stands; 24.00, which is not more than 80.00, so 24.00.
- Payment dated 14 March came back, late fee standing: the payment is after the grace period's last day, so 24.00, held to no more than 80.00.
- A payment not credited toward any due date came back: 24.00 with no limit.
